title: Store and read your first key
summary: Master core Redis string primitives, JSON serialization, and response deserialization.

steps.title: Set a string key with JSON payload
steps.explanation: Redis keys are binary-safe strings up to 512MB. Use the SET command to store a serialized JSON user profile in sandbox DB 15 with the play: prefix.
steps.hint: Click 'Run it for me' or type: SET play:user:101 '{"name":"Alice","role":"admin","credits":50}'

steps.title: Retrieve and inspect the key
steps.explanation: Use GET to fetch the value. In the RESP wire protocol, Redis returns a bulk string prefix ($) followed by length and payload.

steps.title: Inspect internal data type
steps.explanation: Execute TYPE to check how Redis classifies this key. Redis stores strings using raw sds (Simple Dynamic String) or integer encodings.
